# jp-address-search

> Rust library for Japanese address search: postal code (zipcode) to address
> lookup, prefecture and municipality master data, and municipality
> representative points (city-hall coordinates). All data is embedded at
> compile time — zero runtime dependencies, no I/O, no external API.
> 日本の郵便番号検索・住所検索・市区町村の代表点(緯度経度)取得を行う
> Rustライブラリ。データ同梱・依存ゼロ。

## When to use

Use this crate when a Rust application needs, fully offline (no API key, no
network, no database — data ships inside the binary):

- zipcode → address autofill (〒 7-digit Japanese postal code lookup)
- parsing / normalizing a free-form Japanese address string into
  prefecture / municipality / town and its zipcode
- prefecture / municipality master data (JIS X 0401/0402 codes,
  designated-city wards, duplicate-name handling)
- municipality code → representative latitude/longitude (city-hall
  location), e.g. as the origin of a nearby / radius search

Not a fit for: block/lot-level (番地) geocoding, building-level data,
or addresses outside Japan.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
jp-address-search = "0.3"
```

## API

All searches go through the `AddressSearch` entry point
(`use jp_address_search::AddressSearch;`). Return values reference embedded
`'static` data; lookups never allocate.

- `AddressSearch::find_by_zipcode(zipcode: &str) -> &'static [&'static Address]`
  — postal code → addresses. Non-digit characters are ignored ("100-0001" ==
  "1000001"). Input must contain exactly 7 digits, otherwise returns empty.
  One zipcode can map to multiple towns (returns all). ~6ns per lookup.
- `AddressSearch::parse_address(address: &str) -> AddressMatch`
  — parse a free-form address string ("東京都世田谷区太子堂4丁目1-1") by
  longest-prefix matching: prefecture (optional) → city (county name 郡
  optional) → town. Returns `AddressMatch { prefecture: Option<&Prefecture>,
  city: Option<&City>, address: Option<&Address> }` with whichever levels were
  identified. Tolerates whitespace, full-width digits, 大字, and ヶ/ケ/が
  variants. When one town is split into multiple zipcodes by block (丁目),
  the leading number after the town name is matched against each entry's
  `town_note` range (e.g. 大通西25丁目 → 0640820 "20〜28丁目"). Lot numbers
  (番地) are not parsed. Unlisted towns fall back to the city's catch-all
  zipcode entry.
- `AddressSearch::find_addresses_by_city_id(city_id: i32) -> &'static [Address]`
- `AddressSearch::addresses() -> &'static [Address]` — all entries, city-code order.
- `AddressSearch::prefectures() -> &'static [Prefecture]` — all 47, code order.
- `AddressSearch::find_prefecture_by_id(id: i32) -> Option<&'static Prefecture>`
- `AddressSearch::find_prefecture_by_name(name: &str) -> Option<&'static Prefecture>`
  — matches full name ("東京都"), not short name ("東京").
- `AddressSearch::cities() -> &'static [City]` — all municipalities, code order.
- `AddressSearch::find_city_by_id(id: i32) -> Option<&'static City>`
- `AddressSearch::find_city_by_name(name: &str) -> Option<&'static City>`
  — identical city names exist in different prefectures (e.g. 府中市 is in
  both Tokyo 13206 and Hiroshima 34208); the one with the smallest code is
  returned. To disambiguate, filter `find_cities_by_prefecture_id` by name.
- `AddressSearch::find_cities_by_prefecture_id(prefecture_id: i32) -> &'static [City]`
- `AddressSearch::find_city_location(city_id: i32) -> Option<&'static CityLocation>`
  — representative point of a municipality (location of its main government
  office / city hall), for use as an origin of nearby searches. Designated
  cities have both the city itself and each ward. When an office sits outside
  its own municipality (e.g. Taketomi 47381's office is in Ishigaki), the
  actual office location is returned. Returns `None` for the six Northern
  Territories villages (01695-01700), which have no functioning office.
- `AddressSearch::preload()` — optional warm-up; data otherwise loads lazily
  on first access (~10ms).

## Data types (plain structs, public fields)

- `Prefecture { id: i32, name, short_name, en_name: &'static str }`
  — JIS X 0401 code (1-47), "東京都" / "東京" / "tokyo".
- `City { id: i32, prefecture_id: i32, designated_city_id: i32, name: &'static str }`
  — JIS X 0402 5-digit code. `designated_city_id` is the parent city code for
  designated-city wards (e.g. 堺市堺区 27141 → 堺市 27140), 0 otherwise.
- `CityLocation { city_id: i32, latitude: f64, longitude: f64 }`
  — WGS84 decimal degrees of the municipality's main government office.
- `Address { zip: &'static str, prefecture_id, city_id: i32, prefecture_name,
  city_name, town, town_note: &'static str }` — `zip` is 7 digits
  without hyphen. `town` is town-level (町域), empty when the town
  cannot be determined. `town_note` holds the KEN_ALL parenthetical detail
  (block/lot ranges like "1〜19丁目", building floors), empty otherwise.

## Example

```rust
use jp_address_search::AddressSearch;

let addresses = AddressSearch::find_by_zipcode("154-0004");
assert_eq!(addresses[0].prefecture_name, "東京都");
assert_eq!(addresses[0].city_name, "世田谷区");
assert_eq!(addresses[0].town, "太子堂");
```

## Data sources

- Postal codes: Japan Post "KEN_ALL" (utf_ken_all.csv, one record per line).
- Municipalities: Ministry of Internal Affairs "全国地方公共団体コード".
- Municipality locations: MLIT 国土数値情報 "市区町村役場等及び公的集会施設
  データ (P05)".
- Regenerate embedded TSVs with
  `cargo run --features generate --bin update_address` /
  `cargo run --features generate --bin update_master` /
  `cargo run --features generate --bin update_city_location`
  after placing source files under `storage/` (see README).
